reason: Start with the after-meal condition to see how pancreatic cells respond to plentiful glucose.
expectation: I expect beta cells to release insulin into the blood, though the result may first show only sensing.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response also matters, but I prefer to follow the meal-to-fasting sequence.

effect: The result confirms insulin release and identifies muscle and liver as targets, so I can follow either branch.
reaction: The separate target branches make the next choices clear.
reason: Follow insulin to skeletal muscle to see its after-meal effect.
expectation: I expect insulin to increase muscle glucose uptake, possibly with some glucose stored as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: The liver response is also relevant, but I want to follow the muscle branch first.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose entry through more membrane transporters, and its release weakens as glucose falls. The liver branch remains.
reaction: The link between the hormone signal, transporters and feedback is clear.
reason: Follow insulin to the liver to complete the after-meal response.
expectation: I expect the liver to take up glucose and store more of it as glycogen.

alternatives.reason: The between-meals response is also a goal, but I want to finish the after-meal branch first.

effect: The liver stores glucose as glycogen and reduces its glucose output; its glucose entry is not shown using the muscle-style transporter response. The after-meal goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction between the liver and muscle responses is useful.
reason: Follow the only available combination to start the between-meals response.
expectation: I expect pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon as blood glucose falls, signalling the liver to make glucose available.

effect: The between-meal condition increases glucagon release and lowers insulin release, with glucagon directed toward the liver.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal response is clear.
reason: Follow the only available combination to see how the liver maintains blood glucose.
expectation: I expect glucagon to promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release into blood.

effect: Glucagon promotes liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release, then its stimulation diminishes as blood glucose rises. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback loop makes a clear contrast with the after-meal response.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing insulin's effects on muscle and liver was most worthwhile: the picture plans distinguish muscle transporter insertion from liver glycogen storage rather than implying identical responses.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial insulin-release step was fairly predictable, though it clearly established the two target branches.

surprise.text: The explicit distinction that liver glucose entry is not shown with muscle-style transporter insertion refined my expectation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each followed a stated condition or a hormone's target, though the fast menu supplied compatibility.

continue.text: Yes. I would try another chapter for similarly concrete comparisons linking signals, organ responses and feedback, although the compatible-option format makes the choices fairly guided.
